scope: Mail body storage development implementation and deployment

deployment.incident: An initial rollout preceded migration installation; the startup migration guard blocked the API. Migrations were applied through the runner and the API recovered before final validation.

migration.compressionNote: Includes a repetitive synthetic test message; ratio is not representative of real mail.

coverage: Canonical text and HTML round trips and corruption failures
Actor authorization and tenant RLS before object reads
Durable cleanup after rollback and stale-worker fencing
Scheduled delivery and SMTP acknowledgement during a subsequent storage outage
Spam decision and AI source hydration
Body-only search through Meilisearch and current SQL authorization
Legal hold, journal, eDiscovery and retention integration
validation.web: No web source changes; no new browser or accessibility run for this storage change.

postMigrationCheckpoint.scope: Full logical database plus mail body objects; use pre-migration full archive for other objects

restore.scope: Logical database and all mail body objects restored and verified; not a full new-host application recovery.

limits: Development deployment remains development-only; existing production acceptance gaps and upstream vulnerabilities are not closed by this change.
PostgreSQL metadata, drafts, embeddings and retained evidence still grow. Object storage and PostgreSQL share the development host.
Search uses asynchronous token/phrase matching and an explicit 10000-candidate limit per term.
Compressed and expanded bodies are limited to 50 MiB.
Existing journal/review evidence and tenants with active legal holds are conservatively retained inline by backfill.
Rollback requires a body-aware reader or a matched database/object restore; an old inline-only reader is unsafe.
No long-duration load test or full new-host recovery was performed.
Off-server backups currently depend on the operator machine.
